newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian villages say LNG pipes destroy property.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian villages say LNG pipes destroy property.

text.p: More than 100 villages in the southeastern Rivers state have claimed gas pipes laid in building the liquefied natural gas plant (LNG) have destroyed their properties, the state news agency reported on Tuesday.
The News Agency of Nigeria quoted Victor Lesli-Atata, spokesman for the communities, as saying LNG surveyors did not follow the rules during the laying of the gas pipes.

Farms, fish ponds and other properties worth millions of naira were destroyed in the process, Lesli-Atata said, adding: "The NLNG neither paid compensation nor told the villagers what is to become of their destroyed farms and other properties."
The NLNG violated the Oil Pipelines Act of 1956 which guaranteed that adequate and fair compensation should be paid in such circumstances, he said.
Construction work is proceeding on the $4 billion LNG project plant in Bonny which is expected to produce 7.2 billion cubic metres of gas yearly from 1999.
